_comment: Site values (addresses, MACs) are written as their names between double at-signs and filled in from site.local.json (honeypot/site.py). Relative paths are relative to this file. Deployed layout on the Orchestrator mirrors the repo: ~/honeypot/{honeypot/, corpus284_lab_2026-09.json, eval_not_gradable.json}.
_deadline_comment: A model answer is streamed and cut at answer_deadline_s (failover included); a Jetson that sends nothing within first_token_s counts as down. 25 s matches the old timeout, so no answer that used to finish is cut; only the ones that came back empty now return what arrived.
_replay_tier_comment: OFF, and to stay off in the evaluated system (decided 2026-10-08). On, a command typed exactly as in the corpus, with an answer that does not depend on time, boot or session, gets the recorded answer without the model: a lookup of the command text in a table of stored answers, which is the hash-table caching ruled out for the study. Off, those commands go to the model; the corpus is still its retrieval examples and the fine-tuning data. A missing key means off.
_hidden_examples_comment: Corpus entries the relay does not load, so the model is never shown them (decided 2026-10-08): their recorded answers share three or more lines in a row with the answer of a test command. 42 `hostnamectl status` is the whole answer of the test command `hostnamectl`; 233 `printenv | head -15` is 15 of the 21 lines of `env`; 262 is half of /etc/os-release; 263 and 264 are 25 of the 27 lines of /etc/passwd. The relay never reads the test set, so the list is written out here; tests/test_relay.py recomputes it from the recordings and fails if the two differ.
_class_show_withheld_comment: OFF, and off for every measurement in the paper. The class build only (decided 2026-10-15): true shows the model the hidden_examples above again (so `cat /etc/passwd`, `/etc/os-release` and `hostnamectl` are answered from the real lines, not from a line count), and is switched on only after the paper's last measurement, at the freeze. /health then reports withheld_shown, and run43_for_scorer.py, run_leave_one_out.py, measure_build.sh and the rehearsal refuse to measure. The paper says the class build differs in this one respect. A missing key means off.
_answer_mode_comment: normal: code, then model. model_only: every line goes to the model, with the session state in its prompt; code still keeps the state, and what it would have answered is logged next to the model's answer (paper: code vs model on the same commands). Per request: honeypot.mode.
_code_scope_comment: What moved from the model to code on 2026-10-14, one switch per category (accepted by the user 2026-10-14, each switchable in case a category is ruled out of scope). false hands that category back to the model exactly as before that day; a missing key means on. The categories and what each covers: honeypot/shell.py, SCOPE_DEFAULTS. The relay reads this at start: restart it after a change.
_down_comment: A Jetson is given up on when the connection takes longer than connect_s (off or hung; a live one on the lab network answers in a millisecond), when no first token comes within first_token_s, or when it sends nothing for stall_s in the middle of an answer. It then gets no command until a background probe (every 15 s) has seen it answer again, so a dead Jetson costs one command connect_s once, not every command 10 s.
_loop_stop_comment: Since 2026-10-21 (decision log F1, a side build beside build-1018): a generated answer still running after loop_stop_s seconds that ends in a counting loop (12 lines alike except for numbers that each go up by one, or 12 such numbers in one line; backend.counting_loop) is cut there. The fine-tuned 1.7B counted through invented USB devices and RFC numbers until the 25 s deadline (lsusb 5 of 5 runs). No answer recorded on the reference machine has such a run longer than 10 lines, so none would be cut. 0 = off, as in build-1018.
_line_bound_comment: ON since 2026-10-22 (the user's OK after build-1022-bound: corpus answers exact unchanged, answers cut at the 25 s deadline 9 to 4 of 144; decision log F7). The paper's build-1018 had it off. When on: a generated answer to a command that fixes the number of lines it can print is stopped once it holds that many lines (finish_reason lines) and clean() keeps at most that many. Only head or tail as the last command of a single pipeline with -N, -n N, -nN, --lines=N or no count (10), at most one file (shell.line_limit); anything else (-c, -f, +N, -n -N, -q, -v, -z, several files, ; && || redirections, substitutions) is left alone. Generated head/tail answers sometimes ran on to the 25 s deadline. No recorded answer has more lines than its command allows (tests/test_relay.py, TestLineBound).
_node_rest_comment: OFF (0). A rest for a Jetson after each generated answer, as a multiple of the time the answer took: with 2 a node works a third of the time at most. Built 2026-10-13 after a node froze under 46 answers without pauses although its memory was flat, having survived 300 with pauses (docs/jetson-stability.md). While one node rests the other is asked; if both rest, the command waits (20 s at most). It changes how fast a script is answered, so it is the user's to switch on.
_node_spread_comment: ON since 2026-10-13. Each generated answer goes to a node that is generating nothing, and of those to the one idle longest, among the nodes that run the same model. Nothing waits and nothing is slower (two people at once are answered by two nodes instead of queueing on one). A script without pauses then loads each of n nodes 1/n of the time instead of one node all of the time, the load that froze Jetson 1 (docs/jetson-stability.md). It does not by itself prove a node survives such a script: with two nodes each still works about half the time. false gives the old order: the role's node first, the spare only when it fails.
_class_start_comment: First day of the class pen test: 2026-11-02 (set 2026-10-08; was 2026-10-15). This install's setup day (Docker installed, iot-stack created) is placed 3-5 days before it, so 2026-10-28..30 (identity.install_shift_ns). That day only applies once the Orchestrator has been rebooted after it, e.g. at the freeze on the evening of 2026-11-01; while the Orchestrator's boot is older, the setup day is moved back in whole days to lie before the boot, so changing this value alone moves nothing.
_docker_api_comment: The fake Docker API (dockerapi.py), in the relay process so it shares the Docker state with the shell. 127.0.0.1 until it is opened to the lab on purpose.
_backends_comment: Since 2026-10-19 (the user's GO of 18 Oct, decision log E3) every node serves the fine-tuned Qwen3 1.7B, honeypot-ft-1p7b (ollama ID f2e462db45e7 on all four; the paper's base-model build is build-1018, this one sits beside it). Roles (2026-10-02): Jetson 1 answers machine-state and, until Jetson 3 has its Docker model, docker lines; Jetson 4 runs the identical untuned base model as the spare for every role. Jetsons 2 and 3 serve since 2026-10-14 (night), after the three Jetson scripts, with Jetson 1's roles; with node_spread on, a generated answer goes to the node idle longest and roles only order ties. All four hold numerically identical weights (Jetson 1's file has its tensors in another order: docs/jetson-ollama-setup.md).
_substitutions_comment: Ground Truth -> Orchestrator (R1). Read off both machines 2026-09-29 (Orchestrator: ip a, ip -br link). The Orchestrator has no wlan0; its wlan0 MAC is derived as eth0's plus one, the pattern Ground Truth shows. Formal identity recording is plan day 4.
_last_login_comment: What the first login after a relay start shows, until a real login replaces it. Ground Truth's own value after the 2026-09-29 front-door capture.
